text:
Brock Faber returned to the Wild lineup on Nov. 14 after a skull fracture, and on Tuesday he scored in his first home game back, to a loud ovation from the crowd in St. Paul. Three games, three Wild wins, and he's already playing 24.4 minutes a night, which is how much Minnesota needed him.

Three games tell us almost nothing about his season. The five-on-five numbers are poor so far (41.9% of expected goals with him on the ice), and they'll swing a lot as the sample grows. What matters more is that he's back in his usual role, and that Michael Russo's reporting in The Athletic describes the same high standards as before.

Last season sets the bar. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, with the Wild creating more chances when he played. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile for shot attempts among defensemen, though not many from the slot. Watch whether he gets inside more as he finds his legs. A Maple Grove kid, drafted by the Kings, he is Minnesota's top defenseman again.
headline: Faber is back from a skull fracture
